_about: Input data for scripts/build_hardware_report.py. Every figure carries a source and a date. Nothing in the report is typed twice; change a value here and re-run the generator. Confidence: 'tracked' = a named seller's listed price, 'range' = a spread across reputable UAE sellers, 'estimated' = derived or interpolated by the author, 'measured' = measured on a test machine.

locale.note: All prices are AED as listed by UAE sellers, VAT-inclusive. USD appears only where the vendor bills in USD - token APIs and international GPU rental - converted at the 3.6725 peg.

market_context.headline: A DRAM and GDDR shortage driven by AI datacentre buildout is the governing condition on every price in this report.

dram_share_of_supply.value: ~20% of global DRAM capacity absorbed by AI

relief_timeline.value: No meaningful relief forecast before 2028 (Micron HBM capacity)

supply_cuts.value: NVIDIA reportedly considering 30-40% output cuts on mid-range parts to prioritise higher-margin AI silicon

global_street.value: RTX 5090 street pricing USD 4,300-5,000 against a USD 1,999 MSRP; RTX PRO 6000 listed at USD 16,000, up from USD 8,565 at launch

uae_markup.value: UAE retail on an RTX 5090 Founders Edition runs above AED 12,000 against a USD 1,999 (~AED 7,340) MSRP

uae_used_market.value: Dubizzle UAE lists roughly 290 used graphics cards nationally, with a further 91 in Abu Dhabi - a real market, not a handful of listings

rtx_3090_used.label: RTX 3090 24 GB, used
rtx_3090_used.note: Listings seen at AED 2,000 (PNY XLR8) and AED 2,300 (GamingPro). The single AED 9,900 listing is a stale outlier and is excluded.

rtx_4090_used.label: RTX 4090 24 GB, used or renewed
rtx_4090_used.note: AED 8,300 for a sealed ROG Strix on Dubizzle; AED 11,999 for a Gigabyte Gaming OC renewed with warranty at retail. The planning figure sits between the two.

rtx_5090.label: RTX 5090 32 GB, new
rtx_5090.note: AED 13,839 (Gigabyte AORUS special) to AED 22,000 (Founders Edition). ASUS TUF at AED 16,500 is the typical shelf price.

rtx_pro_5000.label: RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 48 GB ECC, new
rtx_pro_5000.note: Get a written quote. Promise Gulf's own product page says AED 15,500 while its price-list page says AED 31,943 for the same card.

rtx_pro_6000.label: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB ECC, new
rtx_pro_6000.note: Adarc AED 48,825, GCC Gamers AED 52,000, Microless AED 58,275, Promise Gulf AED 67,000, Amazon.ae AED 77,032. A 58% spread on one part number.

board_am5.label: X870E ATX, dual x16 slots (x8/x8)
board_am5.note: GIGABYTE X870 class at AED 1,935; entry AM5 boards start near AED 800 but lack the second x16 slot.

board_trx50.label: Gigabyte TRX50 AERO D, sTR5, 4x x16
board_trx50.note: USD 595 at Microless Global plus local margin. Confirm with a UAE quote; sTR5 boards are a special-order item here.

ram_64gb.label: 64 GB DDR5 (2x32)
ram_64gb.note: Kingston Fury Beast RGB 64 GB at AED 1,924 (CostToCost) to AED 4,241 (Microless). Notably cheaper than the global street price for the same shortage.

ram_128gb.label: 128 GB DDR5 RDIMM (TRX50, quad channel)
ram_128gb.note: Interpolated from the tracked 64 GB figure with an RDIMM premium. The least certain line in this report - price it before committing to any TRX50 build.

psu_1200.label: 1200 W 80+ Gold/Platinum
psu_1200.note: Thermaltake Toughpower GT 1200 W listed as low as AED 459.

local_purchase.note: Buying from a UAE seller means the 5% customs duty on CIF has already been paid by the importer and is inside the shelf price. The buyer pays 5% VAT, which is shown separately on the tax invoice and is recoverable by a VAT-registered business. There is no international freight and no Mirsal 2 clearance to arrange.

rental.note: There is no in-region rental of a 48 GB consumer-class card. The cheapest UAE-hosted option capable of the design point is a datacentre H100, which is why the in-region line is both over-specified and roughly four times the global price.

api_prices_usd_per_mtok.note: USD 0.35/M cached input - relevant, because an agent loop re-sends its history every turn.
Input price tracked; output price estimated from the class.

energy.note: DEWA publishes the same progressive slabs for residential and commercial accounts: 0.230 AED/kWh to 2,000 kWh, then 0.280, 0.320 and 0.380 above 6,000 kWh, plus a 0.060 AED/kWh fuel surcharge. A server running continuously sits in the top slab, so 0.440 AED/kWh is the right marginal rate. Cooling adds about a third: a split unit moves roughly three watts of heat per watt it draws.

measured_baseline._source: bench_results.json, measured 2026-09-02 on a temporary RTX 3060 12 GB test machine. That machine is not part of any build in this report and is not counted as an asset; these numbers appear only to check the memory formula against real hardware.
measured_baseline.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060, 12288 MB (temporary test box)
measured_baseline.caveat: Every one of these numbers is a single request at a time on Ollama, which does not batch. They validate the memory model; they do not measure concurrency.

windows.value: vLLM has no native Windows support. The GPU host must run Linux; WSL2 works for development but adds a virtualised memory boundary under load.

agent.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
agent.note: The recommended agent. MoE means it reads about 3B of weights per token, so it decodes at the speed of a small model while reasoning like a large one - which is the whole game on a bandwidth-bound machine.

agent.name: GLM-4.7-Flash
agent.note: 68 GB at FP16, 34 GB at INT8, 17 GB at INT4. Listed among the strongest models that fit inside 32 GB.

agent.name: Qwen3-32B
agent.note: Dense: every parameter is read per token, so it decodes roughly ten times slower than the 30B-A3B on the same card. Included as the counter-example that makes the MoE case.

agent.name: Nemotron Nano 9B
agent.note: The fallback lane. Fits beside everything else and scores well on tool calling for its size.

agent.name: qwen3:8b
agent.note: What the project runs today on the test box. HANDOVER.md: 'We are near the edge of what an 8B holds.'

vision.name: Qwen3-VL-8B
vision.note: The practical single-GPU choice. Native-resolution vision encoder, strong document OCR and table extraction.

vision.name: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B
vision.note: MoE vision model. Worth the slot only if invoice-field extraction becomes the product.

vision.name: Qwen3-VL-4B
vision.note: Fits anywhere. The right first VLM to ship.

vision.name: GLM-4.5V
vision.note: Thinking modes for deep document analysis; heavier than the workload warrants.

asr.name: Whisper Large V3 Turbo (809M)
asr.note: Decoder pruned from 32 layers to 4; about 216x real time, WER 7.75% against 7.4% for full large-v3. Runs in 2-3 GB under faster-whisper rather than the 6 GB a naive load costs.

asr.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT
asr.note: 2,728x RTFx - the fastest self-hostable option for batch throughput. English-first.

asr.name: Voxtral Transcribe 2
asr.note: 5.9% average WER against Whisper's 7.4% - the accuracy leader if transcription quality becomes contractual.

tts.name: Kokoro-82M
tts.note: Runs on CPU. At 82M parameters this is the cheapest slot in the stack and should not be given a GPU until measurement says otherwise.

tts.name: Chatterbox
tts.note: Better prosody, five times the memory. Only if voice quality is a selling point.

charts.name: matplotlib / reportlab
charts.note: Graph generation is a CPU tool. It belongs in app/tools.py next to write_excel as an ordinary Python function, not as a model.

workload_model._about: How 10-20 client organisations becomes a number of in-flight requests. Organisations are not concurrency, and the gap between the two is large enough to change which tier gets bought.
notes: 6,000 prompt tokens per turn is high on purpose: app/agent.py re-sends the whole conversation plus every tool result each step, and TOOL_RESULT_BUDGET is 12,000 characters.
peak_hour_share of 0.20 means a fifth of the day's traffic lands in its busiest hour - a normal office shape, and deliberately pessimistic.
Prefix caching is modelled separately because vLLM's automatic prefix caching maps almost perfectly onto this agent loop's re-send behaviour.
36 months is the amortisation window a finance function will expect for compute hardware, and roughly how long a consumer card stays relevant for inference.
AED 185/hour is a mid-market UAE contract rate for a systems engineer. Operations is charged identically to owning and to renting.
The used-card failure reserve is a real line, not a hedge: there is no warranty on a Dubizzle purchase, so 12% of card cost is set aside per build.
vLLM does not give you the whole card. gpu_memory_utilization of 0.90 is the practical default.
